title: Why Coral Reefs Matter
englishText: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support roughly a quarter of all marine species. These vibrant ecosystems are often called the rainforests of the sea because of their extraordinary biodiversity. Corals themselves are not plants but colonies of tiny animals that form a symbiotic relationship with algae living inside their tissues. The algae provide the coral with food through photosynthesis, while the coral offers the algae a protected home. This delicate partnership, however, is highly sensitive to changes in water temperature. When ocean water becomes too warm, corals expel the algae in a process known as bleaching, which leaves the coral white and vulnerable to starvation. If temperatures do not return to normal quickly, the coral eventually dies. Given that reefs also protect coastlines from storms and support fishing industries that millions of people depend on, their decline threatens far more than marine life alone.

analysis.coreAnalysis: 현황 제시(작은 면적, 큰 생물다양성) → 비유로 중요성 강조 → 공생 관계 메커니즘 설명 → however로 취약성 전환 → 백화 현상 메커니즘 설명 → 결과(죽음) → 결론(해양 생물 이상의 더 큰 가치 위협)으로 이어지는 '현상-메커니즘-위협-결론' 구조.
